entry.title: A 60% win rate can still halve the account: risk of ruin and the Kelly fraction over 5,000 seeded paths
entry.summary: A 60% win rate, and the account can still lose half of itself on the way. That is not a rare streak of bad luck. With a 60% win rate, an average win of 0.8 times the average loss, and 10% of the balance at stake on every trade, 36.860% of 5,000 simulated paths touched half of the starting balance at least once within 200 trades. The 10% is not arbitrary: it is the Kelly fraction for those inputs. Every number below is a calculation from our free in-browser calculator, with the same formulas and the same random seed. It is not a forecast and not trading advice. The model is deliberately simple: every trade is independent, wins b units per unit risked with probability p and loses 1 unit with probability 1 − p, with p and b fixed. So a win multiplies the balance by (1 + b × stake) and a loss …

entry.title: "Stop shouldn't mean close: ending a live-caption session in a Manifest V3 extension without losing the last sentence"
entry.summary: I maintain a browser extension that shows live captions (and translated captions) on top of any tab: a video, a livestream, a web meeting. Audio is captured in the browser, streamed over a WebSocket to a server, and recognised text comes back sentence by sentence. Starting a session got all the attention. Stopping was one line: close the socket. That line was the reason a lot of first sessions ended with an empty screen. This post is about what "Stop" has to mean in a streaming pipeline, and the extra wrinkles a Manifest V3 extension adds. A streaming recogniser sends two kinds of results: partial results: fast guesses that keep changing, good for showing "the app is listening"; final results: settled text.
